DILG BACONC PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www_diiq_qov_pn OPiNlON NO. 08 2024 Ms. ANITA ABARRCOSO anita.abarrcoso@deped.gov.ph Dear Ms. Abarrcoso: This refers to your electronic mail dated November 29, 2023 requesting guidance on whether a candidate for sangguniang barangay member who lost in an election may be appointed as a member of the Lupon within a period of one (I) year after such an election. In reply thereto, attention is respectfully directed to Section 94 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act 7160), thus. "Section 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lost in an Election. - (a) No elective or appointive local Official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless othemise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or-controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. (b) Except for losing candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any government-owned or- controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries." (Emphasis supplied) Parenthetically, Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Actions (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended) provides that: "Section 4. A person who lost in an election (except Barangay election) shall not be eligible for appointment or reemployment to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporation within one year following such election." Accordingly, as a general rule, candidates who lost in any election cannot be appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or-controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries within one year following such an election. However, such prohibition does not apply to losing candidates in barangay elections, as clearly enunciated in the foregoing provisions. Stated differently, if the candidate to "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

be appointed lost in the barangay elections, he may still be appointed to any office in the government even if the same was made within the one-year prohibition. Premised from the foregoing, this Department opines that a candidate for sangguniang barangay member who lost in the recent barangay elections may be appointed as a member of the lupon. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JUAN VICTOR R. LLAMAS Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/JVRL,'LLLS/LRALLD/jam Page 2 of 2
